notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/robots/robodojo-benchmark__robodojo --backend fake; evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by stays null); no hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed. The card's mock_strategy.preferred is upstream-sim, but RoboDojo's TaskEnv needs Isaac Sim 5.1, Isaac Lab and the separately downloaded Assets/ on Linux with a CUDA GPU, so no upstream simulator or sim backend was run. fake.py is the package's pure-Python analytic stand-in for the common dual-X5 policy convention: four command keys (left/right arm joint state, left/right normalized gripper) and a 14-number joint/gripper state observation, with a placeholder reward and no termination. It was not compared with the upstream environment. NOT COVERED: the camera RGB/depth arrays and the full observation dict (vision, state, action, instruction); the 42 task scenes, task-specific rewards and success checks; the ControlSeq/MetaControl queue (upstream TaskEnv.step takes that list, while the Gymnasium bridge passes the policy action dict to the fake); Isaac Sim physics, contacts, friction, deformables and domain randomization; and the arm joint position limits, which live in the downloaded USD asset rather than in the tracked clone, so the fake leaves arm commands unbounded and bounds only the normalized gripper command to 0 to 1. Warnings are the expected ones: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (bookkeeping, no native call), two G7.MAYBE_ABSENT for action_space and observation_space inherited from the external gymnasium.Env base, and seven G8.NO_UNIT for bridge-derived inputs (seed twice, ticks, the four action arrays). There are no G4 warnings and no catalogue requests: only cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the line the last check printed.
